request.user:
Assess structural quality only (subject length, a clear call to action, scannable body). This is advisory; be lenient and do not penalise legitimate creative variation.
Subject: Your winter guide — plus 30% off everything this week
CTA: Shop 30% Off — Winter Gear -> https://shop.example.com/winter-guide?discount=30
Body: Winter trips have their own logic. Shorter days, slower miles, heavier packs. You already know this. So we'll skip the preamble and get to what matters.

This week, everything is 30% off — no exceptions, no exclusions. If you've been sitting on a decision about a shelter, insulation layer, or any piece of kit for the cold months, this is the week to move on it.

A few things worth thinking through before your next winter outing:

**Layering that actually works.** Base layers move moisture; mid layers trap air; shells block wind and precipitation. None of them work alone. Know the temperature range you're planning for and build from there.

**Sleep system math.** A bag or quilt rated to 15°F is designed for 15°F conditions with a proper pad underneath. R-value on your sleeping pad matters as much as your bag rating — cold ground pulls heat faster than cold air.

**Pack weight vs. pack warmth.** Winter loads run heavier. That's just true. Plan for it rather than fighting it.

**Moisture management.** Sweat is the enemy in winter. Pace yourself. Vent before you're wet. Dry gear at camp whenever you can.

Everything in our catalog is 30% off through the end of the week. Browse by category, build your kit, and get out there.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object, no prose or code fences. Reason first, then decide — the verdict must follow from the reasoning. Use exactly this key order: {"reasoning": "<one sentence>", "evidence": ["<short quote or fact>", ...], "score": <float 0-1>, "verdict": "pass"|"fail"}.
